_comment: Grafana Alerting file-provisioning format (apiVersion 1): two always-on
growth/health rules -- call failure rate high, push failure rate high --
reading the textfile exporter in this directory (pqp-api-metrics-exporter.py).
Unlike grafana-alert-rules-event.json (which is imported before an event and
deleted after), these are meant to run continuously alongside pqp-api-logs
and pqp-sfu-box. Everything in this repo's Grafana stack is managed by hand
in the UI (docs/MONITORING.md: 'the UI is the source of truth'), so treat
this file the same way -- paste it into Alerting > Alert rules > 'Import from
file' (or POST to /api/v1/provisioning/alert-rules), not as something CI
sources, the Grafana Cloud Prometheus stack the pqp-sfu-box dashboard uses).
BOTH rules carry a volume floor inside the query: `expr and (volume > 20)`
returns nothing when traffic is below the floor, so a single failure at 3am
against near-zero volume never pages. noDataState is OK for the same reason:
no calls / no push in the window is not an incident. Install the exporter
first, or they sit on 'no data' (which, being OK here, is silent).

annotations.summary: More than half of voice-join attempts are being refused.
annotations.description: (attempts - connected) / attempts > 0.5 for 10m, with more than 20 attempts in the window. Break it down by pqp_api_call_join_refused_total{reason}: room-full is the mesh cap (the MoonKase shape), transport-unsupported a client that cannot run the room's media path, no-access/blocked/timeout the moderation gates. See the pqp Growth dashboard.

annotations.summary: More than a quarter of push sends are failing.
annotations.description: failed / (sent + failed) > 0.25 for 15m, with more than 20 send outcomes in the window (pruned excluded -- a dead token is normal GC, not a failure). A sustained spike is a bad APNs/FCM key, an unshared service account, or a vendor outage, per services/push.ts. Break it down by pqp_api_push_delivery_total{platform,outcome}.
